title: Citizen Science Records of Threatened Chelonians Along the Turkish Coast: Observer Structure, Spatial Patterns and Conservation Implications
content:
ABSTRACT

Citizen science (CS) platforms have become global tools for generating both data and awareness for marine megafauna monitoring. This study evaluated CS data for three chelonians (Caretta caretta, Chelonia mydas, Trionyx triunguis) along the Turkish coastline, where tourism pressure and biodiversity coexist. The GBIF application programming interface (API) was utilized as a global aggregator to map the diverse CS platforms active in Türkiye. Subsequently, via native iNaturalist API, spatial analyses were conducted, and latent ecological information was extracted by combining platform metadata with systematic photo re-annotation. Although iNaturalist dominated the GBIF human-observation records (n = 418), native API extraction retrieved more observations than GBIF aggregation (358 vs. 289), including key metadata unavailable through standard GBIF pipelines. Re-annotation of iNaturalist photographs yielded vitality assessments for 92.9% of records (a 3.2-fold increase over platform coverage), with 97.8% concordance. A pronounced seasonal observation peak in summer and the dominance of transient foreign visitors, who contributed 74.0% of observations, confirmed the structural vulnerability to tourism-driven observer dynamics. Loggerhead and Nile softshell turtles were clustered around known nesting and estuarine habitats, while green turtles were recorded at a median of 500.3 km from eastern Mediterranean nesting sites. Green turtle density hotspots confirmed the Fethiye–Göcek SPA as a known foraging area, extending into Datça–Bozburun and Kaş–Kekova SPAs, suggesting potential foraging habitats further west. Stranding events (n = 32) were spatially decoupled from live encounters, identifying the Aegean as a pronounced mortality zone with 68.8% of strandings in advanced decomposition states. Systematically processed CS observations yield conservation-relevant signals spanning platform capacity, participation structure, habitat use and mortality zones.
